result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.description: Evergreen Bank implementation M2 (Build & integration, USD 60,000): PM reports ~80% complete at 3/31 (DOC-0199), but no signed customer acceptance and UAT not started. Under the SOW (DOC-0047) the customer has no obligation to pay and obtains no rights to the deliverable before acceptance, so the performance obligation is unsatisfied and no over-time/percentage-of-completion revenue is recognized in March (would have been ~USD 48,000 if measured on progress). No entry posted; recognition expected on M2 acceptance targeted late April. Logged for controller visibility.

args.text:
MEMO - March 2026 Close
To: Controller
From: David Murguia, Senior Accountant
Subject: ASC 606 revenue recognition - Evergreen Bank implementation project (US entity)

1. CONTRACT AND FACTS
- SOW dated 2026-01-12 (DOC-0047): fixed fee USD 120,000, with 50% (USD 60,000) payable in advance on signature, non-refundable. Three milestones, each a distinct deliverable separately accepted:
    M1 Solution design           30%   USD 36,000
    M2 Build & integration       50%   USD 60,000
    M3 UAT & go-live acceptance  20%   USD 24,000
- Revenue terms: each milestone is earned only upon the customer's WRITTEN ACCEPTANCE of that deliverable. The customer has no obligation to pay for, and obtains no rights to, a deliverable before acceptance.
- Advance invoiced on INV-1030 (DOC-0049), collected 2026-01-20 and correctly deferred via JE-00072 (Dr 1000 / Cr 2200 USD 60,000). Deferred revenue (2200) balance at 3/31 before my entry: USD 60,000 credit, all relating to this contract.
- M1: signed acceptance certificate dated 2026-03-14 (DOC-0184) - "Customer hereby accepts the M1 deliverable in full," signed by D. Whitfield, VP Operations, Evergreen Bank.
- M2: PM email 2026-03-27 (DOC-0199) - build ~80% complete, customer UAT not started, nothing signed, acceptance targeted late April.
- M3: not started.
- The monthly Evergreen subscription (INV-2114, USD 6,200, account 4000) is separate from this SOW and was already recorded; no change.

2. ASC 606 ANALYSIS
Step 2 - Performance obligations: the three milestones are explicitly distinct deliverables that are separately accepted, so each is a separate performance obligation (ASC 606-10-25-19).
Step 4 - Allocation: the contract states a stated, substantive price per milestone (30/50/20 of USD 120,000), which corresponds to standalone value; no reallocation is required.
Step 5 - Timing: the over-time criteria in ASC 606-10-25-27 are not met. In particular, Halvard does not have an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date - the SOW is explicit that the customer owes nothing and obtains no rights to a deliverable prior to acceptance. Control therefore transfers at a POINT IN TIME, evidenced by the customer's written acceptance (ASC 606-10-25-30, indicators of transfer of control). Accordingly, revenue is recognized per milestone on acceptance, not on percentage of completion.

3. MARCH REVENUE RECOGNIZED
M1 only - USD 36,000, supported by the signed 3/14 acceptance certificate. Because the customer has already paid a USD 60,000 non-refundable advance sitting in deferred revenue, the M1 fee is released from the contract liability rather than billed; no contract asset / unbilled receivable (1300) arises and no new AR is recorded.

JE-00305, dated 2026-03-31 (US, USD):
    Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue                       36,000.00
        Cr 4200 Professional Services Revenue                36,000.00
Memo: Evergreen Bank implementation - recognize M1 Solution design revenue (accepted 2026-03-14); release from deferred revenue per SOW.
Support attached: DOC-0047 (SOW), DOC-0184 (signed M1 acceptance), DOC-0049 (advance invoice), DOC-0199 (M2 status).
Because the entry exceeds the USD 10,000 senior accountant posting limit (Policy Manual DOC-0005 s.1), approval was requested immediately after posting; JE-00305 is pending controller approval.

4. AMOUNTS DELIBERATELY NOT RECOGNIZED
- M2 (USD 60,000): no revenue in March despite ~80% physical completion. A progress-based measure would have produced roughly USD 48,000, but with no signed acceptance, no started UAT, no enforceable right to payment and no customer rights to the deliverable, the performance obligation is unsatisfied. Recognizing it would be unsupported. Logged as EXC-001 for your visibility; expect recognition when acceptance is signed (targeted late April).
- M3 (USD 24,000): work not started, no revenue.
Contract revenue recognized to date: USD 36,000 of USD 120,000. Remaining deferred revenue on this contract after JE-00305: USD 24,000 credit in account 2200 (the unearned portion of the advance), with a further USD 60,000 of the contract price still to be billed/earned on M2 and M3.

5. CHECKLIST
US "Revenue recognition" marked in_progress - this project is complete; other US revenue streams remain to be reviewed. No entries were posted to force any balance to agree.
